item.title: Organic farming has lower yield stability
item.description: A team of researchers has investigated how organic and conventional agriculture differ in terms of yield stability over several years.

item.title: Robots enable bees and fish to talk to each other
item.description: Swiss researchers were able to get two extremely different animal species located far apart to interact with each other and reach a shared decision with the help of robots.

item.title: New method makes the experience of sleeplessness more visible
item.description: A Dutch study shows that it is the period after falling asleep that determines whether or not people experience sleep.

item.title: How digitalization drives new water technologies
item.description: Research, innovation, education and entrepreneurship contributes to the development of new technologies in the water sector according to a new report.

item.title: Hearing like a dinosaur
item.description: Alligators use neural maps to localize the source of a sound the same way birds do. A new study suggests that dinosaurs also used this strategy.

item.title: How alpine streams work
item.description: A Swiss study shows that until now, scientists have been substantially underestimating how quickly gases are exchanged between mountain streams and the atmosphere.

item.title: Copenhagen’s biowaste may become steaks
item.description: A new project will develop technology for extracting protein from organic waste, which can be used as a protein supplement for humans or in animal feed.

item.title: Smarter drug release thanks to control over encapsulation
item.description: Dutch researchers have discovered the parameters that govern the encapsulation of drugs.

item.title: Melanin as a new diagnosis and treatment tool for tumors
item.description: German scientists created melanin-loaded cell membrane derived nanoparticles, which improved tumor imaging in an animal model while also slowing the growth of the tumor.

item.title: Examining the highly organized lives of long-distance commuters
item.description: A Swiss scientist took a look at the strategies commuting parents use for managing their time wisely and dealing with unexpected challenges.
